scenes.text: So far, our AI apps only run on our own laptop. [1] Today, we turn one into a real web app, with a link you can share with anyone. [2] Let's deploy your AI app, for free.

[1] We'll use Streamlit, which turns a Python script into a web page. [2] Import Streamlit, and the AI library. [3] Add a title. [4] Read the API key from Streamlit's secrets, never from the code, and create the client. [5] Add a text box, and an Ask button. [6] When clicked, show a spinner, and call the model. [7] Then write the answer on the page. [8] Run it locally, and it opens in your browser!

Now, let's put it online. [1] Add a requirements file, listing streamlit and anthropic. [2] Push your code to GitHub. [3] Sign in to Streamlit Community Cloud, and pick your repository. [4] Paste your API key into the app's secrets settings. [5] Click deploy, and share your link!

Where can you host it? [1] Free platforms, like Streamlit Community Cloud, or Hugging Face Spaces, are perfect for demos, and learning. [2] Paid cloud servers give you more power, custom domains, and control, for real products.

Before sharing publicly, protect yourself. [1] Set a monthly spending limit, in your AI provider's console. [2] Add a simple limit on how many questions each visitor can ask. [3] And keep your API key only in secrets, never in GitHub.

Here are four terms. [1] Deploy, putting your app on a server, so others can use it. [2] Requirements file, the list of libraries the server installs. [3] Secrets, private settings like API keys, stored safely by the host. [4] And rate limit, a cap on how often someone can use it.

Here's a common mistake. [1] People deploy, share the link, and forget about it. [2] If the link goes viral, or bots find it, your AI bill can explode overnight. Set limits, and check usage regularly.

data.myth: Deploy it, share it, forget it.
data.fact: A viral link or bots can explode your bill overnight. Set limits and watch usage.
